label: Institution
name: CBS Films
summary:
CBS Films, established in 2007 as CBS Corporation's film production and distribution division, is a relatively small studio created to leverage CBS's television brand in theatrical film production — notable primarily for films such as The Woman in Black (2012, starring Daniel Radcliffe), The Dictator (2012, Sacha Baron Cohen), and a handful of other mid-budget films before restructuring in 2013 reduced its independent production profile.

CBS Films was founded as CBS Corporation CEO Les Moonves sought to expand the media company's revenue streams beyond television into theatrical film distribution, following other major broadcasters' attempts at studio creation. The venture was managed by Amy Baer and later Lincoln Bandlow. CBS Films acquired and produced a mix of horror films, comedies, and dramas targeting mid-budget theatrical audiences — The Woman in Black with Daniel Radcliffe performing his post-Harry Potter image transition was the most commercially successful CBS Films release.

The venture illustrated the challenges facing traditional broadcasters entering the competitive theatrical film market against established studios. After early commercial results were mixed, CBS Films transitioned primarily to acquisitions and limited production rather than full-scale studio operations. CBS Corporation's 2019 merger with Viacom creating ViacomCBS (subsequently Paramount Global) rendered the CBS Films imprint largely redundant within a company that now includes Paramount Pictures. CBS Films remains a minor footnote in the history of broadcaster-studio ventures, notable primarily for its post-Harry Potter Radcliffe horror film.
